title: Static entanglement structure and adiabatic Bell-state preparation in the tripartite quantum Rabi model
authors: Li-Li Gao, Zi-Xuan Chen, Long-Jie Li, Zi-Cheng Liu, A-Long Zhou, Chuan-Cun Shu, Zi-Min Li
abstract: The tripartite quantum Rabi model couples two qubits to a bosonic mode through a collective spin-oscillator interaction, providing a simple setting for studying two-qubit entanglement. In the zero-detuning limit, the triplet part of the spectrum splits into branches with zero and maximal entanglement, while the antisymmetric singlet ladder remains exactly decoupled. Within the triplet sector, finite detuning turns the crossings between these branches into avoided crossings and redistributes this entanglement. We identify an eigenbranch whose entanglement grows from nearly zero to a nearly maximal value through such avoided-crossing mixing. The weak-coupling level ordering yields a simple analytic criterion for whether this eigenbranch has a separable weak-coupling endpoint. A three-state effective model explains how the Bell-state component becomes dominant as the coupling increases. We further use a finite-time linear ramp of the collective coupling to benchmark the final coupling and ramp time required for high Bell-state fidelity. These results show how collective spin-oscillator coupling reorganizes spectral entanglement and connects static branch structure to finite-time Bell-state preparation.
summary: The paper analyzes the tripartite quantum Rabi model to understand how entanglement evolves when two qubits interact with a shared oscillator mode. By tracking spectral changes through avoided crossings, it demonstrates that this coupling mechanism can guide the system adiabatically toward high-fidelity Bell states. The findings provide both static criteria and practical benchmarks for realizing such entangled states in physical quantum platforms.
main_problem: The study investigates the static entanglement structure and the feasibility of adiabatic Bell-state preparation within the tripartite quantum Rabi model.
main_result: The collective spin-oscillator coupling reorganizes spectral entanglement, allowing for an eigenbranch whose entanglement grows from near zero to nearly maximal values through avoided crossings. This analysis also benchmarks the required parameters for high-fidelity state preparation in finite time.
method: The authors analyze the system spectrum by projecting onto fixed-number oscillator states and developing effective Hamiltonians, comparing static adiabatic tracking with finite-time ramp protocols.
model_or_system: The model is the tripartite quantum Rabi model (TQRM), which couples two qubits to a bosonic mode via a collective spin-oscillator interaction. The Hamiltonian involves terms coupling spins ($\sigma_{x}^1\sigma_{x}^2$) and the oscillator ($a, a^\dagger$).
key_observables: Two-qubit entanglement (quantified by Concurrence), Bell states fidelity, spectral entanglement structure.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\epsilon$), coupling strength ($g$), bosonic frequency ($\omega$), and ramp time ($T$). Key regimes include the zero-detuning limit and weak/strong coupling limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes approximations such as projecting onto fixed-$n$ oscillator indices (Franck-Condon approximation) to derive effective Hamiltonians for tractability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the TQRM coupling structure in different bases, show static entanglement evolution across varying couplings ($g$), and compare analytic predictions from fixed-$n$ models against exact spectral tracking results.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and analyzes its zero-detuning limit. It then develops effective Hamiltonians for the triplet sector using displaced-oscillator frames. The core analysis tracks entanglement evolution across coupling strengths, culminating in a finite-time benchmark protocol for Bell state preparation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how collective interactions mediate quantum information transfer (entanglement) between discrete spin systems and bosonic modes, which is highly relevant to trapped ion or cavity QED platforms.
